article.title: Why ‘Top 10%’ Does Not Always Mean the Same Customers
article.why: Understand why a relative rank can contain different people each year.

paragraphs.en:
A company may call its highest-spending customers the ‘top 10%.’ This sounds like a clear group, but the customers inside it can change every year. Top 10% describes a position in a population. It does not describe a fixed set of people.

Imagine a company has 1,000 customers in 2025. The 100 customers with the highest annual spending are the top 10%. In 2026, the company again selects the highest 100 customers. Some may be the same, but others may be new. A customer who was ranked 80th last year may fall to 150th. Another customer may rise from 200th to 70th.

The spending threshold can change too. Last year, a customer may have needed 500,000 yen to enter the top 10%. This year, the cutoff may be 550,000 yen because customers spend more overall. Or it may fall if the population changes. Therefore, being in the top 10% does not always mean the same level of spending.

This matters when analysts compare years. If top-10% customers spent more this year, we cannot immediately say that last year’s best customers became stronger. The group may contain different people. New high spenders may have entered while some old high spenders dropped out.

A useful analysis can show both the rank and the movement of individual customers. Analysts can ask how many customers stayed in the top 10%, how many moved up, how many moved down, and how the spending cutoff changed. A transition table can make these movements easy to see.

Relative ranks are useful because they summarize where customers stand compared with others. But they should not be confused with a permanent customer segment. When comparing years, always ask two questions: ‘How did the rank change?’ and ‘Are we talking about the same customers?’
paragraphs.zh:
公司每年都可以定義消費最高的10%為 top 10%，但其中的人不一定相同。Top 10%描述的是相對位置，而不是固定顧客集合。某位顧客去年排名80，今年可能掉到150；另一位則可能從200升到70。進入top 10%的消費門檻也可能隨整體消費或population改變。

因此，今年top 10%的平均消費較高，不代表去年的高價值顧客都變強了，可能只是成員更替。跨年分析時應同時看stay、move up、move down與cutoff變化，並確認比較的是否為同一批顧客。
paragraphs.ja:
毎年「上位10％」を作っても、その中の顧客が同じとは限りません。top 10%はpopulation内の相対的位置であり、固定された顧客集合ではありません。昨年80位だった顧客が今年150位になったり、200位だった顧客が70位へ上がったりします。上位10％に入る利用額thresholdも年によって変わります。

そのため今年のtop 10%の平均利用額が高くても、昨年の優良顧客が全員成長したとは言えません。stay、move up、move down、cutoff変化を確認し、同じ顧客を比較しているかを見ることが重要です。

vocabulary.usage: A rank is a relative position.
It is not a fixed set of people.
A rank is not a permanent segment.

business.term: The top decile is a relative group, so we should check member turnover across years.
business.explanation: 跨年度比較相對rank時提醒確認成員更替。

sources: Quantile ranking and longitudinal customer transition analysis.
